topics.label: Introduction to the Cancer Biology Lecture Series
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture series, outlines learning objectives, and frames the fundamental questions of cancer biology.

topics.label: Cancer as a Failure of Cellular Differentiation and Tissue Architecture
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the genetic, epigenetic, and architectural mechanisms through which cancer disrupts normal multicellular differentiation, along with the models used to study them.

topics.label: Invasion, Metastasis, and Distinguishing Benign from Malignant Tumors
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how invasion and metastasis define malignant progression and how these processes are recognized clinically and histologically.

topics.label: Colorectal Adenoma-to-Carcinoma Progression Model
topics.groupedBecause: It uses colorectal polyps to demonstrate the histological and stepwise morphological progression from a benign adenoma to an invasive adenocarcinoma.

topics.label: Tumor Behavior and Neoplasm Nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: They outline the naming rules and clinical behaviors that define and distinguish benign from malignant neoplasms.

topics.label: Pathophysiological Mechanisms of Cancer Morbidity and Mortality
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the local and systemic mechanisms through which primary and metastatic tumors cause disease and death.

topics.label: Comparative and Epidemiological Incidence of Cancers
topics.groupedBecause: They analyze the incidence and tissue distribution of cancer across human demographics and diverse multicellular animal species.

topics.label: Clinical Principles and Applications of Cancer Screening
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate the clinical importance, histological basis, and relative effectiveness of screening methods for detecting cancers at early stages.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Practical Instructions
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture with a review of learning outcomes and practical session reminders.
